findings.title: Element-loop guard duplicated in three test files with conflicting node sets
findings.description: `ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES` and the AST walk are copied into `test_labels.py` (lines 27-34 and 283-286) and `test_confidence.py` (lines 25-32 and 133-136). `test_import_boundary.py` already has the same check as `_loop_lines` (lines 172-209). The copies disagree. `test_import_boundary.py:179` includes `ast.GeneratorExp`, while the two new copies exclude it on purpose so that the `all(... for category in ...)` generator in `labels.py` is allowed. The same "no element loops" rule therefore means different things in different test modules. Fix: keep one node set and one helper in `test_import_boundary.py`, parametrize it over the vector modules (`confidence.py`, `labels.py`), and put the generator-expression exemption in that one place.

findings.title: `LabelVocabulary.category_ids` is typed `frozenset[int]` but the constructor accepts `set`
findings.description: The field is annotated `frozenset[int]`, so under strict pyright the generated `__init__` rejects sets. The runtime check at line 56 accepts both `set` and `frozenset`, and it needs `# pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance]` to pass. The tests then pass sets with `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` (`test_vocabulary_builds_and_stores_a_frozenset` and `test_equal_vocabularies_are_equal` in `tests/core_model/test_labels.py`). The public signature and the runtime contract disagree. The rest of this module requires exact types (`type(category) is int`), so the simplest fix is to require `frozenset` at runtime, drop the `set` branch, and update those two tests. That removes both suppressions.

findings.title: `_coerce` returns an implicit `None` for an unhandled `ParameterType`
findings.description: `_coerce` handles `INTEGER` and `REAL` in a `match` with no fall-through. Its return type includes `None`, which means "uncoercible". A future `ParameterType` member would therefore return `None` silently. A valid default would fail as "is not a valid <type>", and a valid supplied value would be reported as `wrong_type`. Neither message points at the missing branch, and pyright does not flag it, because `None` is already in the return type. Fix: add `case _: assert_never(parameter_type)` (from `typing`). Pyright then reports the gap when a member is added, and the runtime fails loudly.

findings.title: Vacuous test: `test_match_selects_the_branch_for_each_form`
findings.description: The test runs a `match` in its own body on the output it was given, then asserts on the string the test itself built. It never calls anything in `declarations.py`, so it passes regardless of what the library does with the three output forms. Delete it. The behavior it implies is already covered by `test_declared_order_is_preserved` and `test_declarations_reject`, which includes a non-declaration item at `outputs[1]`.

findings.title: No test pins the int64-extreme ordering that `_require_time_order` depends on
findings.description: Line 117 says subtraction would wrap at the int64 extremes, which is why the code compares neighbours. No test in `tests/core_model/test_signals.py` covers that case. `test_rejects_decreasing_times` (line 146) uses 100, 300, 200. A refactor to `np.diff` would silently accept `[INT64_MAX, INT64_MIN]`, because the difference wraps to a positive value. `tests/core_model/test_series_index.py:252-260` already covers this for `BarIndex`. Add the equivalent `SignalSequence` case.

findings.title: `bind_parameters` accepts `str`-subclass keys that equal a declared name
findings.description: The check `key not in declared` uses `str` hashing and equality, so `np.str_("window")` binds as `window`. The rest of the module requires exact `str`: `require_name` uses `type(value) is not str`, and `canonicalize` rejects non-exact mapping keys. The bound output is keyed by `declaration.name`, so no bad data results. This is an inconsistency. If exact keys are intended, add a `type(key) is str` check; otherwise, say in the docstring that subclasses are accepted.

findings.title: `errors.py` and `declarations.py` depend on each other at the type level
findings.description: `errors.py` imports `ParameterIssue` under `TYPE_CHECKING` from `declarations.py`, which imports `errors.py`. The comment records the intent, and nothing breaks at runtime. The cycle exists only to annotate `InvalidParametersError.issues`. If it grows, move `ParameterIssue` and `ParameterIssueKind` into a module that both can import.

findings.title: `display.py` has no production consumer yet
findings.description: Nothing under `src/` imports `display.py`. In this slice its only effect is the canonicalization-rejection test, and its docstring says the catalog will use it later, which matches D11. Keep it if the catalog slice follows; otherwise it is dead code.

findings.title: Numeric coercion rejects `bool`, NaN, infinity and out-of-range integers
findings.description: Traced `as_integer` and `as_real` by hand. `bool` and `np.bool_` are excluded, `np.float32(5.0)` coerces to `5`, and `2**63` and `2.0**63` return `None` from the int64 range check. `10**400` returns `None` through `as_real`'s `OverflowError` path. The table in `tests/core_model/test_value_checks.py` matches these outcomes.

findings.title: The one broad-scope `try/except` follows the exception rule
findings.description: The `try` catches only `OverflowError`, and the comment explains why `None` is returned rather than raising. This meets rule (b) in the project's exception-handling standard.
